events.enhanced_description: William Petrie excavated at Hawara, finding papyri and a large necropolis with 146 portraits on coffins. His first excavation there proceeded in phases, with the initial work on Amenemhat III’s pyramid postponed until 1889.

image.caption: A limestone model of the Hawara pyramid from the Petrie Museum of Egyptian Archaeology.
image.credit: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin FRCP(Glasg) — Own work
image.date_qualification: Museum object representing the Hawara pyramid; it is not a photograph of Petrie’s excavation. The saved image date is 2016-03-10.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Petrie excavates at Hawara

events.enhanced_description: The Lick Observatory's great telescope, with a 91 cm (36 in) diameter objective lens, was first used, enhancing astronomical observations. This telescope became a pivotal tool for astronomers, contributing to significant discoveries in the field.
events.name: The great telescope at Lick Observatory is first used

events.enhanced_description: The Schoolhouse Blizzard struck the Dakota Territory and several surrounding states, resulting in the tragic deaths of 235 individuals, many of whom were children returning home from school. This blizzard is remembered for its sudden onset and devastating impact.
events.name: The Schoolhouse Blizzard hits Dakota Territory and surrounding states

events.enhanced_description: The National Geographic Society was founded in Washington, D.C., with the aim of increasing and diffusing geographic knowledge. It has since become a leading organization in exploration, education, and conservation.
events.name: The National Geographic Society is founded

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Grapevine Creek marked the last major conflict of the infamous Hatfield-McCoy Feud, a violent family rivalry that captured national attention. This battle exemplified the intense animosity between the two families and the lawlessness of the time.
events.name: The Battle of the Grapevine Creek

events.enhanced_description: The Amateur Athletic Union (AAU) was founded by William Buckingham Curtis in New York City, aiming to promote and develop amateur sports in the United States. The AAU played a crucial role in organizing competitions and establishing standards for various sports.
events.name: The Amateur Athletic Union is founded

events.enhanced_description: The Lawn Tennis Association was founded in London, establishing the framework for the sport of lawn tennis in England. This organization has since been pivotal in promoting tennis and organizing competitions, including the prestigious Wimbledon tournament.
events.name: The Lawn Tennis Association is founded

events.enhanced_description: In West Orange, New Jersey, inventor Thomas Edison met with photographer Eadweard Muybridge, who proposed a groundbreaking scheme for sound film. This meeting highlighted the intersection of photography and motion picture technology during a pivotal time in cinematic history.
events.name: Thomas Edison meets Eadweard Muybridge

events.enhanced_description: The Agriculture College of Utah, which later became Utah State University, was founded in Logan, Utah. This institution has played a significant role in agricultural education and research in the region.
events.name: The Agriculture College of Utah is founded

events.enhanced_description: The death of Wilhelm I marked the end of an era in German history, as his grandson Frederick III ascended to the throne as German Emperor and King of Prussia. Frederick's reign was short-lived, lasting only 99 days due to his untimely death.
events.name: Wilhelm I dies, Frederick III becomes German Emperor

events.enhanced_description: The Great Blizzard of 1888 commenced along the eastern seaboard of the United States, resulting in widespread disruption and the deaths of over 400 people. This storm is remembered for its severity and the challenges it posed to transportation and communication.
events.name: The Great Blizzard of 1888 begins

events.enhanced_description: The catastrophic collapse of the summit of Ritter Island triggered a tsunami that resulted in the deaths of an estimated 500 to 3,500 people. This event underscored the geological volatility of the region and its potential for devastating natural disasters.
events.name: The summit of Ritter Island collapses

events.enhanced_description: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd. was founded in Kimberley, South Africa, marking the beginning of a major player in the diamond industry. This company would go on to dominate the diamond market for decades.

image.caption: De Beers mine shaft, depicted in an image associated with Gardner F. Williams’s The Diamond Mines of South Africa.
image.credit: Gardner F. Williams — The Diamond Mines of South Africa
image.date_qualification: Image date is 1905-01-01, after the company’s 1888 founding; it depicts a mine site, not the founding event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd. is founded

events.enhanced_description: The Sikkim Expedition, a British military operation, commenced with the objective of expelling Tibetan forces from northern Sikkim. This expedition was part of the broader British imperial strategy in the region.

image.caption: Detail from a map of Sikkim showing the principal theatre of war of the Sikkim Expedition.
image.credit: compiled by the Intelligence Branch, Division of Army Chief of Staff, Army Headquarters, India — Paget, William Henry (1907). Frontier and overseas expeditions from India .
image.date_qualification: Map dated 1907, nineteen years after the 1888 expedition.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: The Sikkim Expedition begins

events.enhanced_description: The foundation stone for the new National Library of Greece was laid in Athens, symbolizing a commitment to preserving and promoting Greek culture and literature. This library has since become a vital institution for research and education.
events.name: Foundation stone for the National Library of Greece is laid

events.enhanced_description: The first Romani language operetta premiered in Moscow, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the Romani people. This event marked a significant moment in the recognition and celebration of Romani arts.
events.name: The first Romani language operetta premieres

events.enhanced_description: A pivotal meeting called by William McGregor took place in London to discuss the establishment of The Football League. This meeting laid the groundwork for organized football in England, leading to the formation of the first professional league.
events.name: Meeting to discuss establishment of The Football League

events.enhanced_description: The International Congress for Women's Rights, organized by Susan B. Anthony, opened in Washington, D.C. This congress was a significant milestone in the international women's movement, leading to the formation of the International Council of Women.
events.name: International Congress for Women's Rights opens

events.enhanced_description: Emma Elizabeth Smith, a London prostitute, was brutally attacked by two or three men in Whitechapel, succumbing to her injuries the following day. This incident marked the beginning of the infamous Whitechapel murders, although she is not believed to be a victim of Jack the Ripper.
events.name: Emma Elizabeth Smith attacked

events.enhanced_description: The first New Year's Day was observed in Siam, adopted by King Chulalongkorn, with the 106th anniversary of Bangkok's founding in 1782 as its reference date. This reform marked a significant shift in the cultural practices of the nation.
events.name: First New Year's Day observed in Siam

events.enhanced_description: The Concertgebouw orchestra was inaugurated in Amsterdam, establishing it as one of the leading orchestras in the world. This event marked a significant development in the cultural landscape of the Netherlands.
events.name: Concertgebouw orchestra inaugurated

events.enhanced_description: Kahisakan, the first coffee shop in Japan, opened in Tokyo, introducing a new social and cultural space for the Japanese populace. This establishment played a crucial role in popularizing coffee culture in Japan.
events.name: Kahisakan opens in Tokyo

events.enhanced_description: The German Empire formally annexed the island of Nauru, expanding its colonial territories in the Pacific. This annexation was part of Germany's broader imperial ambitions during the late 19th century.
events.name: German Empire annexes Nauru

events.enhanced_description: Westminster School was founded in Simsbury, Connecticut, establishing a new educational institution that would provide a rigorous academic environment. The school has since become known for its strong academic programs and commitment to student development.
events.name: Westminster School is founded

events.enhanced_description: The Texas State Capitol building was completed and opened to the public in Austin, Texas, at a cost of $3 million. This architectural landmark is notable for its distinctive Renaissance Revival style and serves as the seat of government for the state of Texas.
events.name: Texas State Capitol building opens

events.enhanced_description: The Fort Belknap Indian Reservation was established by the United States Congress in 1888, providing a designated area for the Gros Ventre and Assiniboine tribes. This establishment was part of a broader policy of the U.S. government to manage Native American lands and populations during this period.
events.name: Fort Belknap Indian Reservation is established by the United States Congress

events.enhanced_description: The International Exhibition of Science, Art and Industry opened in Kelvingrove Park, Glasgow, on May 8, 1888, showcasing innovations and artistic achievements from around the world. The exhibition attracted significant public interest and highlighted Glasgow's role as a center of industry and culture during the Victorian era.

image.caption: John Lavery’s oil painting The Fairy Fountain depicts an illuminated fountain at the Glasgow International Exhibition.
image.credit: John Lavery — Bonhams
image.date_qualification: Retrospective illustration of the exhibition; the painting is dated 1888, but the evidence does not establish that it depicts the opening on 8 May.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: The International Exhibition of Science, Art and Industry in Kelvingrove Park, Glasgow opens

events.enhanced_description: The Nippon Oil Corporation, which later became known as Eneos, was founded in Niigata Prefecture, Japan, on May 10, 1888. This establishment marked the beginning of a significant player in Japan's petroleum industry, contributing to the country's energy sector development.
events.name: Nippon Oil Corporation is founded

events.enhanced_description: On May 12, 1888, the territories of the North Borneo Chartered Company, including Sabah, were declared a British protectorate. This move was part of the broader British imperial expansion in Southeast Asia during the late 19th century.
events.name: North Borneo becomes a British protectorate

events.enhanced_description: The Lei Áurea, or Golden Law, was enacted on May 13, 1888, in Brazil, officially abolishing slavery in the country. This landmark legislation was a significant step in the fight for human rights and was championed by Princess Isabel, who was acting as regent at the time.
events.name: Lei Áurea abolishes slavery in Brazil

events.enhanced_description: The comic novel 'The Diary of a Nobody' by brothers George and Weedon Grossmith began serialization in Punch magazine on May 26, 1888. This work is celebrated for its humorous portrayal of middle-class life in Victorian England and has become a classic of English literature.
events.name: The Diary of a Nobody begins serialization

events.enhanced_description: On May 28, 1888, Celtic F.C. played its first official match, defeating Rangers F.C. 5-2. This match marked the beginning of one of the most famous rivalries in football history, known as the Old Firm.
events.name: Celtic F.C. plays its first official match

events.enhanced_description: The Peak Tram in Hong Kong commenced operations on May 30, 1888. This funicular railway has since become a popular tourist attraction, providing stunning views of the city as it ascends to Victoria Peak.

image.caption: The sixth-generation Peak Tram in its classic green livery.
image.credit: Samson Ng . D201@EAL — https://www.flickr.com/photos/64314473@N08/52380931409/
image.date_qualification: Photograph dated 2022-09-07; not a depiction of the tram’s 1888 opening.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Hong Kong's Peak Tram begins operation

events.enhanced_description: On June 2, 1888, Edward King, the Bishop of Lincoln, was called to account for his use of ritualistic practices in Anglican worship. This incident highlighted the tensions within the Church of England regarding traditional versus modern practices.
events.name: Edward King called to account for ritualistic practices

events.enhanced_description: The Kingdom of Sedang was established on June 3, 1888, in what is now modern-day Vietnam. This short-lived kingdom was part of the broader context of colonial expansion in Southeast Asia.

image.caption: Flag of the Kingdom of Sedang.
image.credit: Mysid — Self-drawn in Inkscape, based on FOTW .
image.date_qualification: The flag file is dated 2006-10-23; this is not the depicted date of the 1888 event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: The Kingdom of Sedang is formed

events.enhanced_description: On June 14, 1888, the territories of the White Rajahs in Sarawak were declared a British protectorate. This marked a significant moment in the colonial history of Borneo, as British influence expanded in the region.
events.name: White Rajahs territories become British protectorate

events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 1888, Wilhelm II ascended to the throne as German Emperor and King of Prussia, marking the beginning of his reign during a tumultuous period known as the Year of the Three Emperors. His leadership would significantly influence German and European politics leading up to World War I.
events.name: Wilhelm II becomes German Emperor

events.enhanced_description: The Republican Convention opened on June 19, 1888, at the Auditorium Building in Chicago, where Benjamin Harrison was nominated for President and Levi P. Morton for Vice President. This convention was pivotal in shaping the Republican Party's platform for the upcoming election.
events.name: Republican Convention opens in Chicago

events.enhanced_description: On June 29, 1888, Handel's 'Israel in Egypt' was recorded onto wax cylinder at The Crystal Palace in London, marking the earliest known recording of classical music. This event was significant in the history of music preservation and technology.
events.name: Handel's Israel in Egypt recorded

events.enhanced_description: The Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom opened its laboratory on June 30, 1888, at Plymouth Hoe. This establishment played a crucial role in marine research and the study of marine biology in the UK.
events.name: Marine Biological Association opens laboratory

events.enhanced_description: On July 2, 1888, about 200 matchgirls at the Bryant and May factory in London went on strike following the dismissal of three colleagues. This strike was precipitated by an article on their working conditions published by journalist Annie Besant, marking a significant moment in labor rights history.
events.name: London matchgirls strike of 1888

events.enhanced_description: On July 11, 1888, over 200 miners were killed in a tragic incident at a diamond mine in Kimberley, South Africa. This disaster underscored the dangers faced by workers in the mining industry during this period.
events.name: Over 200 miners killed in Kimberley

events.enhanced_description: On July 15, 1888, a large-scale eruption occurred at Mount Bandai in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, resulting in the deaths of more than 477 people. This catastrophic event highlighted the geological volatility of the region.
events.name: Mount Bandai eruption

events.enhanced_description: On July 25, 1888, Frank Edward McGurrin, a court stenographer from Salt Lake City, Utah, won a typing contest in Cincinnati, Ohio, defeating Louis Traub. This event is often regarded as the birth of the touch typing method, which has become a standard in modern typing.
events.name: Typing contest victory for Frank Edward McGurrin

events.enhanced_description: On August 1, 1888, Carl Benz was issued the world's first driving licence by the Grand Duchy of Baden. This milestone marked a significant development in automotive history and regulation.
events.name: Carl Benz issued first driving licence

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 1888, Bertha Benz completed the first long-distance drive in history, traveling 40 miles (64 km) from Mannheim to Pforzheim in a car manufactured by her husband, Carl Benz. This journey demonstrated the practicality of the automobile and helped to promote its use.
events.name: Bertha Benz completes first long-distance drive

events.enhanced_description: On August 7, 1888, the body of Martha Tabram, a London prostitute, was discovered in Whitechapel, marking one of the earliest suspected murders linked to the infamous Jack the Ripper. The brutal nature of her death raised alarm and heightened fears about the safety of women in the area.
events.name: Whitechapel murders: The body of London prostitute Martha Tabram is found

events.enhanced_description: On August 9, 1888, a devastating fire consumed the Main Building of Wells College in Aurora, New York, resulting in a significant financial loss estimated at $130,000. This incident marked a pivotal moment in the college's history, prompting discussions about rebuilding and modernization.
events.name: Fire destroys the Main Building of Wells College

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 1888, Dr. Friedrich Hermann Wölfert successfully completed the world's first engine-driven flight with his motorised airship, traveling from Cannstatt to Kornwestheim in Germany. This landmark event marked a significant advancement in aviation technology.
events.name: Dr Friedrich Hermann Wölfert’s motorised airship flight

events.enhanced_description: On August 13, 1888, the Local Government Act was enacted, establishing county councils and county borough councils in England and Wales. This legislation not only redefined local governance but also granted women the right to vote in local elections, marking a significant step towards gender equality.
events.name: Local Government Act establishes county councils in England and Wales

events.enhanced_description: On August 20, 1888, a mutiny erupted at Dufile in Equatoria, leading to the imprisonment of Emin Pasha, a notable figure in the region. This event highlighted the tensions and challenges faced by colonial administrators in Africa during this period.
events.name: Mutiny at Dufile results in Emin Pasha's imprisonment

events.enhanced_description: On August 22, 1888, the earliest recorded evidence of a death and injury caused by a meteorite was documented in Sulaymaniyah, Iraq. This incident underscored the potential dangers posed by celestial events and sparked interest in meteorology and astronomy.
events.name: Earliest evidence of death and injury by meteorite in Iraq

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 1888, the first horse-drawn trams began operation in Tallinn, Estonia, then known as Reval. This development marked a significant advancement in urban transportation and contributed to the modernization of the city.
events.name: First trams in Tallinn begin operation

events.enhanced_description: On August 31, 1888, the mutilated body of Mary Ann Nichols was discovered in Whitechapel, London, marking her as the first confirmed victim of the notorious Jack the Ripper. The gruesome nature of her murder intensified public fear and media frenzy surrounding the Ripper case.
events.name: Whitechapel murders: The body of Mary Ann Nichols is found

events.enhanced_description: On September 4, 1888, George Eastman registered the trademark Kodak and received a patent for his innovative camera that utilized roll film. This invention revolutionized photography, making it more accessible to the general public.
events.name: George Eastman registers Kodak trademark and patent

events.enhanced_description: On September 6, 1888, Charles Turner became the first bowler in cricket history to take 250 wickets in a single English season, a remarkable achievement that set a high standard for future cricketers. This milestone is celebrated in the annals of cricket history.
events.name: Charles Turner takes 250 wickets in an English cricket season

events.enhanced_description: On September 8, 1888, The Great Herding (El Gran Arreo) commenced, involving thousands of sheep being herded from Fortín Conesa to Santa Cruz near the Strait of Magellan in Argentina. This event was significant for the region's agricultural development and economy.
events.name: The Great Herding begins in Argentina

events.enhanced_description: On September 17, 1888, Las Cruces College was founded in Las Cruces, New Mexico, which later evolved into New Mexico State University. This institution has played a vital role in higher education in the region.
events.name: Las Cruces College is founded

events.enhanced_description: On September 27, 1888, the 'Dear Boss letter' was received by London's Central News Agency, signed 'Jack the Ripper'. This letter is notable for being the first instance where the name 'Jack the Ripper' was used, further sensationalizing the case.
events.name: Whitechapel murders: The 'Dear Boss letter' is received

events.enhanced_description: On September 30, 1888, the bodies of Elizabeth Stride and Catherine Eddowes were discovered in Whitechapel, London. Stride's body was found first, while Eddowes' mutilated body was found shortly after, marking them as the third and fourth victims of Jack the Ripper.
events.name: Whitechapel murders: Bodies of Elizabeth Stride and Catherine Eddowes are found

events.enhanced_description: The Whitehall Mystery refers to the discovery of dismembered remains of a woman's body at three locations in central London, including the construction site of New Scotland Yard. This gruesome event sparked widespread media attention and speculation about the identity of the victim and the circumstances surrounding her death.
events.name: The Whitehall Mystery

events.enhanced_description: The Washington Monument officially opened to the public on October 9, 1888, becoming a prominent symbol of the nation's capital. Standing at 555 feet, it is the tallest stone structure and obelisk in the world, commemorating George Washington, the first President of the United States.
events.name: Washington Monument Opening

events.enhanced_description: On October 14, 1888, Louis Le Prince filmed the Roundhay Garden Scene, recognized as the first motion picture in history. This brief film, lasting just over two seconds, marked a significant milestone in the development of cinema.
events.name: First Motion Picture Filmed

events.enhanced_description: St Cuthbert's Society was founded at the University of Durham on October 25, 1888, during a meeting chaired by Reverend Hastings Rashdall. This society has since played a significant role in the university's community and student life.
events.name: Foundation of St Cuthbert's Society

events.enhanced_description: On October 30, 1888, King Lobengula of Matabeleland granted the Rudd Concession, allowing exclusive mining rights to Charles Rudd and his associates, acting on behalf of Cecil Rhodes. This agreement laid the groundwork for the colonization and subsequent establishment of Rhodesia.
events.name: The Rudd Concession

events.enhanced_description: In the 1888 United States presidential election held on November 6, Grover Cleveland, the Democratic incumbent, won the popular vote but lost the Electoral College to Republican challenger Benjamin Harrison. This election highlighted the complexities of the American electoral system.
events.name: 1888 United States Presidential Election

events.enhanced_description: On November 8, 1888, Joseph Assheton Fincher filed a patent in the United Kingdom for the parlour game he called 'Tiddledy-Winks.' This game has since become a popular pastime, known for its simple rules and engaging gameplay.
events.name: Patent for Tiddledy-Winks

events.enhanced_description: On November 9, 1888, the mutilated body of Mary Jane Kelly was discovered in Whitechapel, marking her as the fifth and final victim of the infamous Jack the Ripper. This brutal murder intensified public fear and media frenzy surrounding the unsolved case.
events.name: Mary Jane Kelly Murder

events.enhanced_description: On November 16, 1888, Ethiopia began to show the first signs of famine, exacerbated by a severe drought and the early spread of the rinderpest epizootic. This crisis had devastating effects on the agricultural sector and the population.
events.name: Famine Signs in Ethiopia

events.enhanced_description: The first Saint Verhaegen celebration took place in Brussels on November 24, 1888. This event honors the founder of the Université libre de Bruxelles and is a significant cultural tradition in the city.
events.name: First Saint Verhaegen Celebration

events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 1888, the international sorority Delta Delta Delta was founded at Boston University. This organization has since grown to become one of the largest women's fraternities in the United States, promoting sisterhood and philanthropy.
events.name: Delta Delta Delta Founding

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 1888, the celebration of Thanksgiving coincided with the first day of Hanukkah, a rare occurrence that brought together diverse cultural and religious traditions in the United States.
events.name: Thanksgiving and Hanukkah Coincide

events.enhanced_description: On December 7, 1888, John Boyd Dunlop patented the pneumatic bicycle tyre in the United Kingdom, revolutionizing cycling and paving the way for modern tire technology. This invention significantly improved the comfort and performance of bicycles.
events.name: Dunlop's Pneumatic Tyre Patent

events.enhanced_description: The Lyric Theatre in London opened its doors on December 17, 1888, becoming a significant venue for theatrical performances. It has since hosted numerous productions and remains a vital part of London's cultural landscape.
events.name: Lyric Theatre Opening

events.enhanced_description: On December 18, 1888, Richard Wetherill and his brother-in-law Charlie Mason discovered the ancient Indian ruins of Mesa Verde in southwestern Colorado. This discovery contributed significantly to the understanding of Native American history and archaeology.
events.name: Discovery of Mesa Verde

events.enhanced_description: On December 23, 1888, Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh, after a quarrel with fellow artist Paul Gauguin, famously cut off the lower part of his left ear and delivered it to a brothel in Arles. This incident is often cited as a reflection of van Gogh's struggles with mental illness.
events.name: Vincent van Gogh Cuts Off Ear

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1889, a total solar eclipse was visible across parts of California and Nevada. This astronomical event captivated observers and contributed to the growing interest in solar phenomena and the science of astronomy during the late 19th century.

image.caption: Composite photograph of the total solar eclipse, made from plates photographed at different exposures from Norman, California.
image.credit: Washington University eclipse party — H. S. Pritchett (1891). "The solar corona of January, 1889, from the photographs" . Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific 3(16): 155–162. Plate is on unnumbered page preceding the article.
image.date_qualification: Image date stated as 1889-01-01; the composite print is credited to an 1891 publication.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Total solar eclipse of January 1, 1889

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, Wovoka, a Paiute spiritual leader, experienced a vision that led to the formation of the Ghost Dance movement among Native American tribes in the Dakotas. This movement sought to restore Native American culture and bring about a renewal of life, reflecting the struggles faced by indigenous peoples during this period.
events.name: Wovoka experiences a vision leading to the Ghost Dance movement

events.enhanced_description: The influenza pandemic of 1889-1890 was first reported in Bukhara, in the Central Asian part of the Russian Empire. This pandemic spread rapidly across the globe, affecting millions and marking one of the first instances of a worldwide health crisis in modern history.
events.name: Influenza Pandemic Begins

events.enhanced_description: In June 1889, Vincent van Gogh painted 'The Starry Night' while staying at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France. This iconic painting is celebrated for its swirling skies and emotional depth, representing van Gogh's unique artistic vision.
events.name: Vincent van Gogh Paints The Starry Night

events.enhanced_description: In August 1889, the Jewish settlement of Moisés Ville was founded in Argentina, marking a significant moment in Jewish immigration to South America. This settlement became a center for Jewish culture and community life in the region.
events.name: Foundation of Moisés Ville

events.enhanced_description: The first issue of The Wall Street Journal was published in New York City in 1889, marking the beginning of one of the most influential financial publications in the world. It has since played a crucial role in business journalism and financial reporting.
events.name: First issue of The Wall Street Journal published

events.enhanced_description: The last official bare-knuckle boxing title fight took place in Mississippi in 1889, where Heavyweight Champion John L. Sullivan defeated Jake Kilrain in a grueling match that lasted 75 rounds. This event marked the end of an era in boxing, transitioning towards more regulated forms of the sport.
events.name: Last official bare-knuckle boxing title fight

events.enhanced_description: In November 1889, Costa Rica held its first free elections, marking a significant step towards democratic governance in the country. This event laid the foundation for the political development of Costa Rica in the years to come.
events.name: First free elections in Costa Rica

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, German geologist Hans Meyer and Austrian mountaineer Ludwig Purtscheller became the first climbers to reach the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa. Their successful ascent marked a significant achievement in the history of mountaineering.
events.name: Mount Kilimanjaro's summit is first reached

events.enhanced_description: The Moulin Rouge cabaret opened its doors in Paris on January 1, 1889, quickly becoming a symbol of the Belle Époque and a hub for entertainment and artistic expression. It is renowned for its can-can dance and vibrant performances.

image.caption: The Moulin Rouge cabaret in Paris.
image.credit: Christine Zenino — Flickr : Moulin Rouge
image.date_qualification: Photographed 2011-04-23; the image shows the site decades after the 1889 opening.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY 2.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution 2.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: The Moulin Rouge cabaret opens in Paris

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1889, North Dakota and South Dakota were admitted to the United States as the 39th and 40th states, respectively. This admission marked a significant expansion of the United States into the northern Great Plains.
events.name: North Dakota and South Dakota are admitted as the 39th and 40th U.S. states

events.enhanced_description: Wimbledon F.C. played their first match on January 1, 1889, marking the inception of one of the most storied football clubs in England. The club has since become known for its passionate fan base and its unique history.
events.name: English Association football team Wimbledon F.C. plays their first match

events.enhanced_description: Gustav Mahler premiered his Symphony No. 1 in Budapest on January 1, 1889. This work, often referred to as the 'Titan,' showcased Mahler's innovative orchestration and emotional depth, establishing him as a significant composer of the late Romantic era.
events.name: Gustav Mahler premieres his Symphony No. 1

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, yellow fever outbreaks severely disrupted the construction of the Panama Canal, leading to significant delays and loss of life among workers. The disease highlighted the need for improved sanitation and health measures in tropical construction projects.
events.name: Yellow fever interrupts the building of the Panama Canal

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, a massive locust swarm crossed the Red Sea, devastating crops in the Nile Valley of Egypt. This ecological disaster had significant implications for food security and the local economy, exacerbating hardships for the population.
events.name: A huge locust swarm crosses the Red Sea and destroys crops in the Nile Valley

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, Frederick Abel invented cordite, a smokeless propellant that revolutionized artillery and ammunition. This invention significantly improved the effectiveness and safety of firearms and artillery in military applications.
events.name: Frederick Abel invents cordite

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, an early method of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission, developed by Swiss engineer René Thury, was implemented commercially by the Acquedotto de Ferrari-Galliera Company in Italy. This system marked a significant advancement in electrical engineering and power distribution.
events.name: An early method of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission is implemented commercially in Italy

events.enhanced_description: The Capilano Suspension Bridge, the longest suspension footbridge in the world at the time, opened in 1889 in British Columbia, Canada. This engineering marvel became a popular tourist attraction and remains a significant landmark in the region.

image.caption: Photograph of the Capilano Suspension Bridge in Vancouver, Canada.
image.credit: Markus Säynevirta — Own work
image.date_qualification: A photograph of the bridge in 2016, decades after its 1889 opening; it documents the site, not the opening event. No supported display date is available.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: The Capilano Suspension Bridge opens in British Columbia

events.enhanced_description: In 1889, the Wisden Cricketers' Almanack published its inaugural list of Wisden Cricketers of the Year, recognizing six outstanding players for their performances in the previous season. This tradition continues to honor excellence in cricket.
events.name: The Wisden Cricketers' Almanack publishes its first Wisden Cricketers of the Year

events.enhanced_description: On January 4, 1889, President Grover Cleveland signed an act to regulate appointments in the Marine Hospital Service of the United States. This legislation established a Commissioned Corps of officers, laying the groundwork for what would evolve into the modern U.S. Public Health Service.
events.name: An Act to Regulate Appointments in the Marine Hospital Service of the United States

events.enhanced_description: On January 5, 1889, Preston North End F.C. was declared the winner of the inaugural Football League in England. This victory marked a significant milestone in the history of English football, establishing the league as a key component of the sport's structure.
events.name: Preston North End F.C. wins inaugural Football League

events.enhanced_description: On January 8, 1889, Herman Hollerith was granted a patent for his electric tabulating machine in the United States. This invention revolutionized data processing and laid the groundwork for modern computing and information management.
events.name: Herman Hollerith receives a patent for his electric tabulating machine

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 1889, The Coca-Cola Company was originally incorporated as the Pemberton Medicine Company in Atlanta, Georgia. This marked the beginning of what would become one of the most recognized brands in the world, known for its soft drinks and global marketing.
events.name: Incorporation of The Coca-Cola Company

events.enhanced_description: On January 22, 1889, Columbia Phonograph was formed in Washington, D.C. This company played a crucial role in the development of the recording industry and the popularization of phonograph records.
events.name: Formation of Columbia Phonograph

events.enhanced_description: On January 30, 1889, Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria, and his mistress, Baroness Mary Vetsera, were found dead in the Mayerling hunting lodge, leading to speculation about a double suicide or murder-suicide. This tragic event had significant implications for the Habsburg dynasty and European politics.
events.name: Rudolf, Crown Prince of Austria commits suicide

events.enhanced_description: On February 11, 1889, the Meiji Constitution was adopted in Japan, marking a significant step towards modernization and the establishment of a constitutional government. This constitution laid the foundation for Japan's political structure and the convening of the 1st Diet of Japan in 1890.
events.name: Adoption of the Meiji Constitution in Japan

events.enhanced_description: On February 15, 1889, the first issue of La Solidaridad was published in Madrid, Spain. This publication became a significant voice for the Filipino reform movement, advocating for social and political reforms in the Philippines under Spanish colonial rule.
events.name: First issue of La Solidaridad published

events.enhanced_description: On February 22, 1889, President Grover Cleveland signed a bill admitting North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, and Washington as U.S. states. This legislation expanded the United States and marked a significant moment in the country's westward expansion.
events.name: Admission of North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, and Washington as U.S. states

events.enhanced_description: On March 4, 1889, Benjamin Harrison was sworn in as the 23rd President of the United States. His presidency would be marked by significant events, including economic challenges and foreign policy developments.
events.name: Benjamin Harrison sworn in as President of the United States

events.enhanced_description: On March 9, 1889, the Battle of Metemma took place, resulting in the death of Yohannes IV, Emperor of Ethiopia. This battle saw Sudanese forces rally against the Ethiopian army, marking a pivotal moment in the region's history and leading to Menelik II's proclamation as the new emperor.
events.name: Battle of Metemma

events.enhanced_description: On March 11, 1889, the North Carolina Legislature issued a charter for the creation of Elon College. This institution would grow to become Elon University, known for its commitment to liberal arts education and community engagement.
events.name: Charter for Elon College issued

events.enhanced_description: On March 15, 1889, during the Samoan crisis, German and American warships faced off in a standoff in Apia Harbor. The situation escalated until a cyclone struck, sinking several ships and ending the confrontation, highlighting the geopolitical tensions in the Pacific.
events.name: Samoan crisis and cyclone disaster

events.enhanced_description: On March 22, 1889, Sheffield United F.C. was formed at the Adelphi Hotel in Sheffield, England. This club would become one of the prominent teams in English football, contributing to the sport's rich history.
events.name: Formation of Sheffield United F.C.

events.enhanced_description: On March 23, 1889, Mirza Ghulam Ahmad claimed to be the Promised Messiah and Mahdi, founding the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community in Qadian, Punjab. This movement emphasized peace, tolerance, and the reinterpretation of Islamic teachings.
events.name: Founding of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community

events.enhanced_description: On March 31, 1889, the Eiffel Tower was inaugurated in Paris, France, standing at 300 meters tall, making it the tallest structure in the world at the time. Despite initial criticism regarding its design, the tower has become a global icon of France and a symbol of architectural innovation.
events.name: Inauguration of the Eiffel Tower

events.enhanced_description: Following a failed coup attempt against the French government, Georges Boulanger, the French Minister of War, fled to Belgium to escape arrest. His political ambitions and the ensuing scandal marked a significant moment in the political landscape of late 19th-century France.

image.caption: Portrait photograph of General Georges Ernest Boulanger by Atelier Nadar.
image.credit: Adam Cuerden — This file comes from Gallica Digital Library and is available under the digital ID btv1b53151568b/f1
image.date_qualification: Portrait of Boulanger, not a photograph of his flight. The source gives a publication range of 1875–1895 and says it was probably after 1880; no supported display date is available.
image.image_date: Published 1875-1895; probably after 1880 (the year he became a general, since he's named as a general on the paper)
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Georges Boulanger's Flight

events.enhanced_description: The Hammarby Roddförening, later known as Hammarby IF, was established in Stockholm, Sweden, marking the beginning of one of the country's most popular sports clubs. The club has since expanded to include various sports and has a significant following.
events.name: Foundation of Hammarby IF

events.enhanced_description: On April 22, 1889, at high noon, the Land Rush of 1889 commenced in the Oklahoma Territory, leading thousands of settlers to race for land claims. This event resulted in the rapid establishment of towns, including Oklahoma City and Guthrie, and significantly impacted the settlement patterns in the region.

image.caption: Black-and-white photograph print depicting the Land Run for the Northeast Indian Territory.
image.credit: Carl Albert Research and Studies Center, Congressional Collection — http://www.ou.edu/carlalbertcenter/congressional-collection
image.date_qualification: Described as a photograph print of the Land Run on April 22, 1889; the saved image date is 1889-04-22.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: Land Rush of 1889

events.enhanced_description: On May 2, 1889, Menelik II, the Emperor of Ethiopia, signed a treaty of amity with Italy, which granted Italy control over Eritrea. This treaty was significant as it set the stage for future conflicts between Ethiopia and Italy.
events.name: Treaty of Amity with Italy

events.enhanced_description: The Exposition Universelle opened in Paris on May 6, 1889, showcasing innovations and culture from around the world, with the Eiffel Tower serving as its entrance arch. This event celebrated the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution and highlighted France's industrial achievements.

image.caption: View of the Exposition Universelle on the Champ de Mars, photographed from the Eiffel Tower.
image.credit: Neurdein — View of Exposition Universelle from Eiffel Tower, Paris, 1889 - Taken from the Tissandier Collection at the U.S. Library of Congress . …trialsanderrors
image.date_qualification: 1889, as stated in the image date; this is a contemporary view of the exposition, not a ground-level event photograph.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Exposition Universelle

events.enhanced_description: On May 11, 1889, the Wham Paymaster robbery occurred in the Arizona Territory, where a U.S. Army paymaster and his escort were attacked, resulting in the theft of over $28,000. This incident led to the awarding of two Medals of Honor for bravery.
events.name: Wham Paymaster Robbery

events.enhanced_description: On May 28, 1889, Édouard and André Michelin registered their tire company in Clermont-Ferrand, France. This company would go on to become one of the largest tire manufacturers in the world, known for its innovations in tire technology.
events.name: Michelin Company Registration

events.enhanced_description: The Johnstown Flood occurred on May 31, 1889, when the South Fork Dam collapsed, resulting in the deaths of over 2,200 people in and around Johnstown, Pennsylvania. This disaster highlighted the need for improved safety regulations regarding dam construction and maintenance.
events.name: Johnstown Flood

events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 1889, the first long-distance electric power transmission line in the United States was completed, running 14 miles from a generator at Willamette Falls to downtown Portland, Oregon. This milestone marked a significant advancement in electrical engineering and power distribution.
events.name: First Long Distance Electric Power Transmission Line

events.enhanced_description: The Great Seattle Fire occurred on June 6, 1889, devastating the downtown area of Seattle, Washington, but miraculously resulting in no fatalities. The fire prompted a massive rebuilding effort that transformed the city and its infrastructure.
events.name: Great Seattle Fire

events.enhanced_description: The Armagh rail disaster occurred on June 12, 1889, near Armagh, Northern Ireland, resulting in the deaths of 80 people. This tragic event highlighted the dangers of railway travel during that era and led to increased safety measures.
events.name: Armagh Rail Disaster

events.enhanced_description: In June 1889, Raffaele Esposito, a Neapolitan baker, invented the Pizza Margherita, named after Queen Margherita of Savoy. This dish became a symbol of Italian cuisine and is considered the precursor to modern pizza.
events.name: Invention of Pizza Margherita

events.enhanced_description: Bangui was founded in the French Congo on June 26, 1889. It later became the capital of the Central African Republic, playing a crucial role in the region's political and cultural development.
events.name: Foundation of Bangui

events.enhanced_description: The first Inter-Parliamentary Conference was held in Paris on June 29, 1889, bringing together representatives from various countries to discuss international cooperation and peace. This conference laid the groundwork for future diplomatic engagements.
events.name: First Inter-Parliamentary Conference

events.enhanced_description: On July 15, 1889, an assassination attempt was made on Pedro II, the Emperor of Brazil, in Rio de Janeiro. This event underscored the political tensions and instability facing the Brazilian monarchy during this period.
events.name: Assassination Attempt on Pedro II

events.enhanced_description: On July 31, 1889, Louise, Princess Royal of the United Kingdom, married Alexander Duff, 1st Duke of Fife. This marriage strengthened ties between the British royal family and the Scottish nobility.
events.name: Marriage of Louise, Princess Royal

events.enhanced_description: On August 3, 1889, during the Mahdist War, Egyptian and British troops achieved victory in the Battle of Toski. This battle was part of the larger conflict between the Mahdist forces and the Anglo-Egyptian army.
events.name: Battle of Toski

events.enhanced_description: The Great Fire of Spokane occurred on August 4, 1889, destroying approximately 32 blocks of the city. This catastrophic event prompted a significant rebuilding effort, transforming Spokane's urban landscape.
events.name: Great Fire of Spokane

events.enhanced_description: The Savoy Hotel, one of London's most prestigious hotels, officially opened its doors on August 6, 1889. Known for its luxurious accommodations and exceptional service, it quickly became a symbol of elegance and sophistication in the hospitality industry.
events.name: The Savoy Hotel in London opens

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 1889, the Imperial Natural History Museum in Vienna held its grand opening ceremony, showcasing a vast collection of natural history artifacts. The museum attracted 175,000 visitors from August to December of that year, highlighting its immediate popularity and significance in the field of natural sciences.
events.name: Grand opening of the Imperial Natural History Museum

events.enhanced_description: On August 26, 1889, the Prevention of Cruelty to, and Protection of, Children Act, commonly known as the Children's Charter, was enacted in the United Kingdom. This landmark legislation introduced criminal penalties to deter child abuse, marking a significant step forward in child protection laws.
events.name: Children's Charter passed in the UK

events.enhanced_description: The Royal Mail Mount Pleasant Sorting Office officially opened in London on August 30, 1889. This facility became a crucial hub for mail sorting and distribution, significantly improving the efficiency of postal services in the United Kingdom.

locations.name: Royal Mail Mount Pleasant Sorting Office

events.name: Royal Mail Mount Pleasant Sorting Office opens

events.enhanced_description: On September 10, 1889, Albert Honoré Charles Grimaldi ascended to the throne as Albert I, Prince of Monaco. His reign was marked by significant developments in the principality, including advancements in science and culture.
events.name: Albert I becomes Prince of Monaco

events.enhanced_description: On September 15, 1889, dockworkers in London initiated a strike demanding a minimum wage of sixpence an hour, a pivotal moment in the development of New Unionism in Britain. The successful outcome of the strike marked a significant advancement in labor rights and union organization.
events.name: London Dock Strike

events.enhanced_description: On September 17, 1889, Civil War veteran Charles Jefferson Wright founded the New York Military Academy in Cornwall, New York. The academy began with 75 students and has since become a prominent institution for military education.
events.name: Founding of New York Military Academy

events.enhanced_description: On September 23, 1889, Fusajiro Yamauchi founded Nintendo Koppai in Kyoto, Japan, initially to produce and market Hanafuda playing cards. This company would eventually evolve into one of the most recognized names in the global gaming industry.
events.name: Foundation of Nintendo Koppai

events.enhanced_description: The first International Conference of American States commenced on October 2, 1889, in Washington, D.C. This conference aimed to promote cooperation and peace among the nations of the Americas, laying the groundwork for future diplomatic relations.
events.name: First International Conference of American States

events.enhanced_description: On October 6, 1889, German geologist Hans Meyer and Austrian mountaineer Ludwig Purtscheller successfully reached the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro for the first time. This achievement marked a significant milestone in the exploration of Africa's highest peak.

image.caption: View of Mount Kilimanjaro from Amboseli National Park, Kenya.
image.credit: Sergey Pesterev — Own work Alternative: https://unsplash.com/photos/DWXR-nAbxCk Sergey Pesterev
image.date_qualification: A 2012 view of the mountain, not a photograph of the 1889 first ascent.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: CC BY-SA 4.0; UsageTerms: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0; Copyrighted: True

events.name: First ascent of Mount Kilimanjaro

events.enhanced_description: On October 12, 1889, Gustaf Åkerhielm, previously the Swedish Foreign Minister, took office as Prime Minister of Sweden. His leadership was characterized by efforts to modernize the Swedish government and improve international relations.
events.name: Gustaf Åkerhielm becomes Prime Minister of Sweden

events.enhanced_description: On October 21, 1889, Helmuth von Moltke the Elder was recorded by Adelbert Theodor Wangemann using a phonograph, making him the earliest-living human whose voice was captured on wax cylinders. This technological advancement marked a significant moment in the history of sound recording.

image.caption: Franz Goedecker’s Vanity Fair caricature of Helmuth von Moltke the Elder, captioned “Modern Strategy.”
image.credit: Franz Goedecker — Published in Vanity Fair , 23 August 1884. Downloaded from http://www.philaprintshop.com/images/vf82384.jpg
image.date_qualification: The caricature was published on 23 August 1884, five years before the recording on 21 October 1889.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Helmuth von Moltke recorded on phonograph

events.enhanced_description: On October 24, 1889, Sir Henry Parkes delivered the Tenterfield Oration, a pivotal speech calling for the Federation of Australia. This address is often credited with galvanizing support for the movement towards unifying the Australian colonies.
events.name: Tenterfield Oration by Sir Henry Parkes

events.enhanced_description: On October 29, 1889, the British South Africa Company was granted a Royal Charter, allowing it to operate in southern Africa. This charter played a crucial role in the expansion of British colonial interests in the region.
events.name: British South Africa Company receives Royal Charter

events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 1889, North Dakota and South Dakota were admitted as the 39th and 40th states of the United States, respectively. This event marked a significant expansion of the Union and the development of the Great Plains region.
events.name: North Dakota and South Dakota admitted as states

events.enhanced_description: The lynching of Orion Anderson on November 8, 1889, in Leesburg, Virginia, was a racially charged event that highlighted the pervasive violence against African Americans in the post-Reconstruction era. This incident drew attention to the ongoing struggles for civil rights and justice in the United States.
events.name: Lynching of Orion Anderson

events.enhanced_description: On November 8, 1889, Montana was admitted as the 41st state of the United States. This event was part of the broader westward expansion and development of the American frontier.
events.name: Montana admitted as a state

events.enhanced_description: On November 11, 1889, Washington was admitted as the 42nd state of the United States. This admission was a significant milestone in the history of the Pacific Northwest and the expansion of the United States.
events.name: Washington admitted as a state

events.enhanced_description: On November 14, 1889, pioneering journalist Nellie Bly (Elizabeth Cochrane) embarked on her journey to travel around the world in less than 80 days, inspired by Jules Verne's novel. She completed the journey in 72 days, 6 hours, and 11 minutes, breaking records and capturing the public's imagination.
events.name: Nellie Bly begins journey around the world

events.enhanced_description: On November 15, 1889, Field Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca led a military coup that deposed Emperor Pedro II of Brazil, effectively abolishing the Brazilian monarchy. This coup marked the transition of Brazil from an empire to a republic.
events.name: Military coup in Brazil

events.enhanced_description: On November 17, 1889, the Brazilian Imperial Family was forced into exile in France following the military coup that abolished the monarchy. This marked the end of over 60 years of imperial rule in Brazil.
events.name: Brazilian Imperial Family forced into exile

events.enhanced_description: On November 19, 1889, the modern-day flag of Brazil was adopted by the Provisional Government of the Republic. This flag symbolizes the new republican ideals and the transition from monarchy to a democratic government.
events.name: Modern Brazilian flag adopted

events.enhanced_description: On November 20, 1889, Argentina became the first nation to officially recognize Brazil's transition from a monarchy to a republic, following the Brazilian Republic's declaration earlier that month. This recognition was significant in strengthening diplomatic relations between the two South American countries.
events.name: Argentina is the first country to recognize the abolition of the monarchy in Brazil

events.enhanced_description: On November 23, 1889, the first jukebox was installed at the Palais Royale Saloon in San Francisco, California. This invention revolutionized the music industry by allowing patrons to select and play their favorite songs, paving the way for the modern music experience.
events.name: The first jukebox goes into operation, at the Palais Royale Saloon in San Francisco

events.enhanced_description: Clemson University was founded on November 27, 1889, in Clemson, South Carolina, as a land-grant institution. Established by Thomas Green Clemson, the university has since grown into a major research institution known for its engineering and agricultural programs.
events.name: Clemson University is founded in Clemson, South Carolina

events.enhanced_description: On December 14, 1889, Wofford College and Furman University faced off in the first intercollegiate football game in South Carolina. This historic match marked the beginning of college football in the state and contributed to the growth of the sport in the region.
events.name: Wofford and Furman play the first intercollegiate football game, in the state of South Carolina

events.enhanced_description: On December 23, 1889, Recreativo de Huelva was established, becoming the oldest football club in Spain. The club has a rich history and is recognized for its contributions to the development of football in the country.
events.name: The Spanish football team Recreativo de Huelva is formed

events.enhanced_description: On December 28, 1889, the Newark and Granville Street Railway began operations in Ohio, marking the introduction of the first interurban tram-train in the United States. This innovation facilitated transportation between cities and contributed to the expansion of urban areas.
figures: Newark and Granville Street Railway founders
events.name: The first interurban tram-train to emerge in the United States is the Newark and Granville Street Railway in Ohio

events.enhanced_description: On December 30, 1889, Sultan Abdul Hamid II enacted the anti-slave trade law known as the Kanunname of 1889 in the Ottoman Empire. This law aimed to combat the slave trade and improve the legal status of individuals within the empire.
events.name: Abdul Hamid II introduces the anti-slave trade law of Kanunname of 1889

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1890, the Kingdom of Italy formally established Eritrea as its colony in the Horn of Africa. This marked the beginning of Italian colonial rule in the region, which would last for several decades.
events.name: The Kingdom of Italy establishes Eritrea as its colony in the Horn of Africa

events.enhanced_description: American journalist Nellie Bly completed her groundbreaking round-the-world journey in just 72 days in 1890, a feat that captured the public's imagination and demonstrated the possibilities of travel and journalism. Her adventure was inspired by Jules Verne's novel 'Around the World in Eighty Days.'

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Nellie Bly completes her round-the-world journey

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, Preston North End retained the English Football League Championship by winning their final game against Notts County. This achievement solidified their status as one of the leading football clubs of the time.

locations.name: Notts County, Nottinghamshire, England, United Kingdom

events.name: Preston North End retain the English Football League Championship

events.enhanced_description: The Arcade in Cleveland, Ohio, opened in 1890 as one of the first indoor shopping malls in the United States, featuring a stunning five-story skylight that illuminated the grand space. This architectural marvel combined elements of Victorian design with modern commercial functionality, becoming a significant cultural landmark in the city.
events.name: The five-story skylight Arcade opens in Cleveland, Ohio

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, Japan held its first general election for the House of Representatives under the new Meiji Constitution, allowing about 5% of the adult male population to participate. This election marked a significant step towards modern democracy in Japan, reflecting the country's rapid political transformation during the Meiji Restoration.
events.name: First general election for the House of Representatives of Japan

events.enhanced_description: The Ouija board was first released by Elijah Bond in 1890, marketed as a mystical tool for communication with spirits. This novel product quickly gained popularity, becoming a cultural phenomenon and a staple of American spiritualism.
events.name: Release of the Ouija board

events.enhanced_description: In November 1890, the headquarters of the Metropolitan Police Service, known as Scotland Yard, relocated to a new building on Victoria Embankment, which became known as New Scotland Yard, symbolizing a new era in policing in London.
events.name: New Scotland Yard moves

events.enhanced_description: The first Army–Navy Game took place at West Point, New York, where the United States Navy triumphed over the United States Army with a score of 24-0, establishing a long-standing tradition in American college football.

locations.name: West Point, New York, United States

events.name: First Army–Navy Game

events.enhanced_description: Robert Gair, a printer from Brooklyn, invented the folding carton box, revolutionizing packaging and contributing significantly to the paperboard box industry, which began to flourish in the late 19th century.
events.name: Invention of the folding carton box

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, Boise, Idaho, became the site of the first geothermal well drilled in the United States, marking the beginning of geothermal energy exploration and utilization in the region.
events.name: First geothermal well in Boise

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, brown trout were introduced into the upper Firehole River within Yellowstone National Park, an event that had significant ecological impacts on the park's aquatic ecosystems.

locations.name: Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming, United States

events.name: Introduction of brown trout in Yellowstone

events.enhanced_description: John Philip Sousa composed 'High School Cadets' in 1890, contributing to the rich tradition of American military and school band music.
events.name: High School Cadets by Sousa

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, William II of Prussia opposed Otto von Bismarck's attempt to renew the law that outlawed the Social Democratic Party, signaling a shift in German politics and the decline of Bismarck's influence.
events.name: William II opposes Bismarck

events.enhanced_description: The Blackwall Buildings, a noted philanthropic housing project, were constructed in the East End of London in 1890, reflecting the social reform movements of the time aimed at improving living conditions for the poor.
events.name: Construction of Blackwall Buildings

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, English archaeologist Flinders Petrie conducted the first scientific excavation at Tell el-Hesi, mistakenly identified as Tel Lachish, pioneering methods in archaeology and contributing to the understanding of ancient settlement patterns in the Holy Land.
events.name: Flinders Petrie's excavation

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, American geostrategist Alfred Thayer Mahan published 'The Influence of Sea Power upon History, 1660–1783', a seminal work that profoundly influenced naval strategy and international relations in the 20th century.
events.name: Mahan's publication

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, Francis Galton announced a statistical demonstration of the uniqueness and classifiability of individual human fingerprints, laying the groundwork for modern forensic science and identification methods.
events.name: Galton's fingerprint study

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, the Japanese tractor and iron pipe brand Kubota was founded in Osaka, Japan, marking the beginning of a significant player in the agricultural and industrial sectors.
events.name: Founding of Kubota

events.enhanced_description: Emerson Electric, an American electronics industry giant, was founded in 1890 in St. Louis, Missouri, and has since become a leader in various technology and engineering sectors.
events.name: Founding of Emerson Electric

events.enhanced_description: On January 2, 1890, Alice Sanger made history by becoming the first female staffer in the White House. Her appointment marked a significant step towards gender equality in the workplace and opened doors for women in government roles.
events.name: Alice Sanger becomes the first female staffer in the White House

events.enhanced_description: On January 11, 1890, the United Kingdom issued an ultimatum to Portugal, demanding the withdrawal of Portuguese forces from the territory between Mozambique and Angola, which encompassed much of present-day Zimbabwe and Zambia. This event heightened tensions between the two colonial powers.

image.caption: Map of Portuguese southern Africa and surrounding regions, coordinated by A. A. d’Oliveira.
image.credit: Oliveira, Antonio Augusto de (18..-19..?). Auteur du texte — Bibliothèque nationale de France
image.date_qualification: Map dated 1886, four years before the ultimatum of 11 January 1890.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: 1890 British Ultimatum

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 1890, the ballet The Sleeping Beauty, with music composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, premiered at the Imperial Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg, Russia. This classic ballet has since become a staple of the ballet repertoire worldwide.

image.caption: Photograph of Margot Fonteyn and Robert Helpmann performing in The Sleeping Beauty during a Sadler’s Wells Ballet US tour.
image.credit: Sol Hurok/Sadler's Wells Ballet — EBAY front back
image.date_qualification: This is a later performance photograph, not a photograph of the 1890 premiere. The supplied image date identifies a Boston Globe publication date in 1950, not necessarily when the photograph was taken; display date is unsupported.

image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Ballet The Sleeping Beauty premieres at the Imperial Mariinsky Theatre

events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 1890, the United Mine Workers of America was founded in Columbus, Ohio, to advocate for the rights and welfare of coal miners. This organization played a crucial role in labor movements and the fight for workers' rights in the United States.

image.caption: Five coal miners in a railroad car preparing to descend into a mine in Hazelton, Pennsylvania.

events.enhanced_description: On February 5, 1890, Allianz, a global insurance and financial services company, was founded in Berlin, Germany. The company has since grown to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world.
events.name: Allianz is founded in Berlin, Germany

events.enhanced_description: The National American Woman Suffrage Association (NAWSA) was established to advocate for women's voting rights in the United States, uniting various suffrage organizations under a common goal. This pivotal organization played a crucial role in the eventual passage of the 19th Amendment, granting women the right to vote.
events.name: The National American Woman Suffrage Association (NAWSA) is founded

events.enhanced_description: In 1890, Chicago was chosen to host the 1893 Columbian Exposition, a world's fair that celebrated the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus's arrival in the New World. This event showcased the city's recovery from the Great Fire of 1871 and highlighted American innovation and culture.
events.name: Chicago is selected to host the Columbian Exposition

events.enhanced_description: On March 3, 1890, Ohio State University played its first official American football game against Ohio Wesleyan University in Delaware, Ohio. This marked the beginning of a storied football program that would grow to become a significant part of American collegiate sports.
events.name: The first American football game in Ohio State University history

events.enhanced_description: The Forth Bridge, an iconic cantilever railway bridge, was opened to rail traffic on March 4, 1890. This engineering marvel spans the Firth of Forth in Scotland and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, symbolizing the industrial age's advancements in construction.

locations.name: Forth Bridge, South Queensferry, Scotland, United Kingdom

events.name: The Forth Bridge is opened to rail traffic

events.enhanced_description: North Dakota State University was founded in Fargo on March 8, 1890, initially established as a land-grant institution. It has since grown into a major research university, contributing significantly to education and agriculture in the region.
events.name: North Dakota State University is founded

events.enhanced_description: On March 17, 1890, the Randtram, the first railway in the Transvaal region, opened between Boksburg and Braamfontein in Johannesburg. This development marked a significant advancement in transportation and commerce in the burgeoning gold mining region.
events.name: The first railway in Transvaal opens

events.enhanced_description: On March 20, 1890, Kaiser Wilhelm II forced Otto von Bismarck to resign as Chancellor of Germany, marking a significant shift in German politics. Bismarck's departure ended an era of Realpolitik and set the stage for a more aggressive foreign policy under Wilhelm II.
events.name: Kaiser Wilhelm II forces Otto von Bismarck to resign

events.enhanced_description: The March 1890 middle Mississippi Valley tornado outbreak resulted in 24 significant tornadoes, with one particularly devastating tornado striking Louisville, Kentucky, and killing 76 people. This event highlighted the destructive power of tornadoes in the region.
events.name: March 1890 middle Mississippi Valley tornado outbreak

events.enhanced_description: Washington State University was founded in Pullman on March 28, 1890, initially established as a land-grant university. It has grown into a prominent research institution, contributing to various fields of study and serving a diverse student body.
events.name: Washington State University is founded

events.enhanced_description: Kashihara Shrine, a significant Shinto shrine, was officially built by Emperor Mutsuhito (Emperor Meiji) in 1890. The shrine is dedicated to the first emperor of Japan, Emperor Jimmu, and serves as a symbol of Japan's imperial heritage.
events.name: Kashihara Shrine is officially built

events.enhanced_description: The First International Conference of American States was held in Washington, D.C., on April 14, 1890, leading to the establishment of the Commercial Bureau of the American Republics. This conference aimed to promote cooperation and trade among the nations of the Americas.
events.name: The First International Conference of American States

events.enhanced_description: On May 1, 1890, a coordinated series of mass rallies and one-day strikes occurred across many cities and mining towns in Europe and North America, advocating for an eight-hour workday. This event marked a significant moment in the labor movement, emphasizing workers' rights and better working conditions.
events.name: A coordinated series of mass rallies and strikes for an eight-hour workday

events.enhanced_description: On May 2, 1890, President Benjamin Harrison signed the Oklahoma Organic Act, which organized the Oklahoma Territory and laid the groundwork for its future statehood. This act was a significant step in the westward expansion of the United States.
events.name: President Benjamin Harrison signs the Oklahoma Organic Act

events.enhanced_description: The first official English County Championship cricket match took place on May 12, 1890, in Bristol, where Yorkshire defeated Gloucestershire by eight wickets. This match marked the beginning of a structured county cricket competition in England.
events.name: The first official English County Championship cricket match

events.enhanced_description: In May 1890, Dutch artist Vincent van Gogh moved to Auvers-sur-Oise, where he was cared for by Dr. Paul Gachet. During his time there, he created around seventy paintings in just as many days, marking a prolific period in his artistic career before his tragic death.
events.name: Vincent van Gogh moves to Auvers-sur-Oise

events.enhanced_description: The Ulm Minster, located in Ulm, Germany, was inaugurated on May 31, 1890, as the world's tallest cathedral. This Gothic masterpiece is renowned for its stunning architecture and remains a significant landmark in Germany.
events.name: The Ulm Minister opens as the world's tallest cathedral

events.enhanced_description: On June 1, 1890, the United States Census Bureau began utilizing Herman Hollerith's tabulating machine, a groundbreaking innovation that used punched cards to process census data. This technology laid the foundation for modern computing and data processing.
events.name: The United States Census Bureau begins using Herman Hollerith's tabulating machine

events.enhanced_description: Royal Dutch Petroleum was founded in the Netherlands on June 16, 1890, to develop an oilfield in Pangkalan Brandan, North Sumatra. This company would eventually evolve into Royal Dutch Shell, one of the largest energy companies in the world.
events.name: Royal Dutch Petroleum is founded

events.enhanced_description: Oscar Wilde's novel 'The Picture of Dorian Gray' was published in June 1890 by Lippincott's Monthly Magazine in Philadelphia. The story explores themes of vanity, moral duplicity, and the relationship between beauty and morality, becoming a classic of English literature.
events.name: The Picture of Dorian Gray is published

events.enhanced_description: On June 27, 1890, Canadian-born boxer George Dixon defeated the British bantamweight champion in London, claiming the title and becoming recognized as the first black world champion in any sport. His victory was a significant milestone in boxing history.
events.name: George Dixon defeats the British bantamweight champion

events.enhanced_description: The Heligoland–Zanzibar Treaty, signed in 1890, marked a significant shift in colonial power dynamics, with Britain ceding the Heligoland islands to Germany in exchange for control over Zanzibar and Wituland. This treaty not only solidified German colonial ambitions but also reflected the strategic interests of both empires in Africa.
events.name: Heligoland–Zanzibar Treaty

events.enhanced_description: In August 1890, Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany and Tsar Alexander III of Russia met in Narva, Estonia, to discuss diplomatic relations and military cooperation. This meeting was part of broader efforts to stabilize relations between the two empires during a period of rising tensions in Europe.
events.name: Meeting of Kaiser Wilhelm II and Tsar Alexander III

events.enhanced_description: On July 2, 1890, the Sherman Antitrust Act was enacted, representing a pivotal moment in U.S. legal history as it aimed to combat monopolistic practices and promote fair competition. Alongside it, the Sherman Silver Purchase Act sought to increase the amount of silver purchased by the government, reflecting the economic tensions of the era.
events.name: The Sherman Antitrust Act and Sherman Silver Purchase Act become United States law

events.enhanced_description: Idaho was officially admitted as the 43rd state of the United States on July 3, 1890, following a period of rapid population growth and settlement. This admission marked a significant expansion of the American frontier and reflected the ongoing development of the western United States.
events.name: Idaho is admitted as the 43rd U.S. state

events.enhanced_description: On July 10, 1890, Wyoming became the 44th state of the United States, notable for being the first state to grant women the right to vote. This progressive move set a precedent for women's suffrage in the nation and highlighted Wyoming's unique role in American history.
events.name: Wyoming is admitted as the 44th U.S. state

events.enhanced_description: The Sea Wing disaster occurred on July 13, 1890, when a sudden storm capsized the passenger steamboat Sea Wing on Lake Pepin, resulting in the tragic loss of 98 lives. This maritime disaster highlighted the dangers of navigation on the Great Lakes and prompted discussions on safety regulations.
events.name: Sea Wing disaster

events.enhanced_description: The Revolution of the Park took place on July 26, 1890, in Buenos Aires, leading to the resignation of President Juárez Celman. This political upheaval was fueled by widespread discontent with the government and marked a significant moment in Argentine history, paving the way for future political reforms.
events.name: Revolution of the Park

events.enhanced_description: Vincent van Gogh, the renowned Dutch painter, died on July 29, 1890, two days after shooting himself in Auvers-sur-Oise, France. His tragic death marked the end of a tumultuous life and a prolific artistic career, leaving behind a legacy that would profoundly influence modern art.
events.name: Death of Vincent van Gogh

events.enhanced_description: On August 6, 1890, William Kemmler became the first person to be executed in the electric chair at Auburn Prison in New York. This event marked a controversial moment in the history of capital punishment in the United States, raising ethical questions about the methods of execution.
events.name: First execution in the electric chair

events.enhanced_description: The BOVESPA stock exchange was founded on August 23, 1890, in São Paulo, Brazil, marking a significant development in the country's financial landscape. This institution has since evolved into one of the largest stock exchanges in Latin America, facilitating investment and economic growth.

image.caption: Exterior of the Bovespa building in São Paulo.
