events.name: British Nimrod Expedition sets sail

events.enhanced_description: In 1908, the Collinwood school fire near Cleveland, Ohio, resulted in the tragic deaths of 174 individuals. This disaster raised awareness about fire safety in schools and led to changes in regulations to protect students.
events.name: Collinwood School Fire

events.enhanced_description: In 1908, the Bank of Communications was founded in Beijing, China, becoming one of the major financial services providers in the country. It played a significant role in the development of China's banking sector.
events.name: Founding of Bank of Communications

events.enhanced_description: The Ford Model T was officially launched in 1908, with the first unit rolling off the assembly line at the Ford Piquette Avenue Plant in Detroit on September 27. This revolutionary vehicle would change the automotive industry and American society.
events.name: Official launch of Henry Ford's Ford Model T automobile

events.enhanced_description: In 1908, the Penny Post system was established, allowing for affordable mail service between the United Kingdom and the United States. This development significantly improved communication between the two nations.
events.name: Penny Post is established between the United Kingdom and United States

events.enhanced_description: The play 'The Melting Pot' by Israel Zangwill premiered in Washington, D.C. in 1908, quickly becoming a symbol of the American immigrant experience and the idea of cultural assimilation.
events.name: The Melting Pot, a play by Israel Zangwill, opens in Washington, D.C.

events.enhanced_description: In 1908, the Hoover Company of Canton, Ohio, acquired the manufacturing rights to the upright portable vacuum cleaner patented by James M. Spangler on June 22. This acquisition marked the beginning of Hoover's dominance in the vacuum cleaner market.
events.name: Hoover Company acquires rights

events.enhanced_description: A total solar eclipse was visible in the Pacific Ocean, marking the 46th solar eclipse of Solar Saros 130. This astronomical event captivated observers and contributed to the study of solar phenomena.
events.name: Total solar eclipse visible in the Pacific Ocean

events.enhanced_description: On January 13, 1908, a devastating fire broke out at the Rhoads Opera House in Boyertown, Pennsylvania, resulting in the tragic deaths of 171 people. The incident highlighted the need for improved fire safety regulations in public buildings across the United States.
events.name: Rhoads Opera House Fire

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 1908, Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc. was founded at Howard University in Washington, D.C., becoming the first sorority established by African American women. This organization aimed to promote sisterhood and service among its members and has since played a significant role in advocating for civil rights and social justice.

locations.name: Howard University, Washington, D.C., United States

events.name: Founding of Alpha Kappa Alpha

events.enhanced_description: On January 24, 1908, Robert Baden-Powell's book 'Scouting for Boys' was published in London, marking the inception of the global Boy Scout movement. The book provided a framework for youth development through outdoor activities and community service, influencing millions of young people worldwide.
events.name: Publication of Scouting for Boys

events.enhanced_description: On February 1, 1908, King Carlos I of Portugal and his son, Prince Luis Filipe, were assassinated in Lisbon during a politically motivated attack. This event marked a significant turning point in Portuguese history, leading to increased political instability and the eventual establishment of the Portuguese Republic.
events.name: Lisbon Regicide

events.enhanced_description: On February 3, 1908, Panathinaikos A.O., one of the most storied multi-sport clubs in Greece, was founded in Athens. The club has since become a symbol of Greek sports and culture, particularly known for its football team and its green and white colors.
events.name: Founding of Panathinaikos A.O.

events.enhanced_description: On February 12, 1908, the first around-the-world car race, the New York to Paris Race, commenced. This event showcased the capabilities of early automobiles and captured the public's imagination, highlighting the burgeoning automotive industry.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: 1908 New York to Paris Race

events.enhanced_description: On February 18, 1908, the United States enforced the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1907, which restricted Japanese immigration to the U.S. This agreement was a response to rising anti-Japanese sentiment and aimed to ease tensions between the two nations.
events.name: Gentlemen's Agreement of 1907

events.enhanced_description: On February 29, 1908, the State Normal and Industrial School for Women was established in Harrisonburg, Virginia, which later became James Madison University. This institution played a crucial role in the education of women in the region.

locations.historical_name: State Normal and Industrial School for Women
locations.name: Harrisonburg, Virginia, United States

events.name: Founding of State Normal and Industrial School for Women

events.enhanced_description: In March 1908, a 40,000-year-old Neanderthal boy skeleton was discovered at Le Moustier in southwest France by Otto Hauser. This significant find contributed to the understanding of human evolution and the existence of Neanderthals.
events.name: Discovery of Neanderthal Skeleton

events.enhanced_description: On March 4, 1908, the Pretoria branch of Transvaal University College was established, which later evolved into the University of Pretoria. This institution has played a vital role in higher education in South Africa.
events.name: Establishment of Pretoria branch of Transvaal University College

events.enhanced_description: On March 9, 1908, Football Club Internazionale was founded in Milan, Italy. The club has since become one of the most successful and popular football teams in the world.
events.name: Founding of Football Club Internazionale

events.enhanced_description: On March 23, 1908, American diplomat Durham Stevens was assassinated in San Francisco by two Korean immigrants. This act was a response to his support for Japanese expansion in Korea and highlighted the tensions surrounding U.S.-Japan-Korea relations.
events.name: Assassination of Durham Stevens

events.enhanced_description: On March 27, 1908, the first Scout troop outside the United Kingdom was formed in Gibraltar. This event marked the expansion of the Scouting movement beyond British borders.
events.name: First Scout Troop Outside the U.K.

events.enhanced_description: On March 29, 1908, French aviator Henri Farman made history by completing the world's first flight with a passenger, Léon Delagrange, in Paris. This milestone in aviation demonstrated the potential for human flight and paved the way for future advancements in aeronautics.
events.name: First Flight with a Passenger

events.enhanced_description: On April 8, 1908, H. H. Asquith of the Liberal Party took office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Sir Henry Campbell-Bannerman. His leadership would be marked by significant political and social changes in the UK.

locations.historical_name: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
locations.name: United Kingdom

events.name: H. H. Asquith Becomes Prime Minister

events.enhanced_description: On April 20, 1908, the Sunshine rail disaster occurred in Melbourne, Australia, when two trains collided, resulting in 44 fatalities and over 400 injuries. This tragic event prompted a review of railway safety protocols in Australia.
events.name: Sunshine Rail Disaster

events.enhanced_description: On April 21, 1908, explorer Frederick Cook claimed to have reached the North Pole, a statement that would later be contested. His assertion fueled public interest in polar exploration and the race to the Arctic.
events.name: Frederick Cook Claims to Reach North Pole

events.enhanced_description: On October 31, 1908, the Franco-British Exhibition was held in London, showcasing the cultural and industrial achievements of both France and the United Kingdom. This event fostered goodwill and cooperation between the two nations.
events.name: Franco-British Exhibition

events.enhanced_description: On May 26, 1908, a major commercial oil discovery was made at Masjed Soleyman in southwest Persia, marking the beginning of the oil industry in the Middle East. The rights to this resource were quickly acquired by the United Kingdom, significantly impacting global energy markets.
events.name: Discovery of Oil in Persia

events.enhanced_description: Women's Sunday, held on June 21, 1908, was a significant mass demonstration in London organized by suffragettes advocating for women's right to vote. The event drew thousands of participants and highlighted the growing momentum of the women's suffrage movement in Britain.
events.name: Women's Sunday

events.enhanced_description: On June 29, 1908, the Kohlerer-Bahn, designed by engineer Hans Bleichert, opened in Bolzano, South Tyrol. This cable car was the first modern aerial enclosed cable car dedicated solely to passenger service, revolutionizing mountain transport.
events.name: Kohlerer-Bahn opens

events.enhanced_description: On June 30, 1908, the Tunguska event occurred near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Siberia, resulting from the air burst of a large meteoroid or comet fragment. This explosion flattened approximately 2,000 square kilometers of forest and remains one of the largest impact events in recorded history.

locations.name: Podkamennaya Tunguska River, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia

events.name: Tunguska event

events.enhanced_description: On July 1, 1908, the SOS distress signal was officially adopted internationally for maritime communication. This signal, which is easy to recognize in Morse code, became a vital tool for ships in distress.
events.name: SOS distress signal adopted

events.enhanced_description: On July 3, 1908, Major Ahmed Niyazi led a revolt against the Ottoman Empire by defecting from the 3rd Army Corps in Macedonia. This marked the beginning of the Young Turk Revolution, which aimed to restore the constitution and modernize the empire.
events.name: Young Turk Revolution begins

events.enhanced_description: On July 6, 1908, American explorer Robert Peary embarked on an expedition to the North Pole. This journey was part of his long-standing quest to reach the Arctic's northernmost point, which he would claim to have achieved in 1909.
events.name: Robert Peary sets sail for the North Pole

events.enhanced_description: On July 8, 1908, French aviator Léon Delagrange made history by taking his partner, sculptor Thérèse Peltier, on the world's first flight with a female passenger. This event marked a significant milestone in the history of aviation.
events.name: First flight with a female passenger

events.enhanced_description: On July 11, 1908, the steamship Amalthea, which was housing British strikebreakers in Malmö harbour, was bombed by Anton Nilson. The attack resulted in one death and twenty injuries, highlighting the tensions during labor disputes in Sweden.
events.name: Bombing of the steamship Amalthea

events.enhanced_description: On July 11, 1908, the Western University of Pennsylvania was officially renamed the University of Pittsburgh. This change reflected the institution's growth and its commitment to higher education in the region.
events.name: University of Pittsburgh renamed

events.enhanced_description: From July 13 to October 29, 1908, the 1908 Summer Olympics were held in London, originally scheduled for Rome but relocated due to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 1906. This edition of the Games featured a wide range of sports and was notable for its organization and participation.
events.name: 1908 Summer Olympics held

events.enhanced_description: On July 19, 1908, Feyenoord was founded in Rotterdam, Netherlands. This club would go on to become one of the most successful football teams in Dutch history, winning numerous national and international titles.
events.name: Feyenoord football club founded

events.enhanced_description: On July 23, 1908, the Committee of Union and Progress (CUP) issued an ultimatum to Sultan Abdul Hamid II, demanding the restoration of the constitution of 1876. The Sultan complied the following day, marking a significant moment in the Young Turk Revolution.
events.name: Young Turk Revolution ultimatum

events.enhanced_description: On July 24, 1908, Italian runner Dorando Pietri won the Olympic marathon, which started at Windsor Castle and ended in London. His dramatic finish, where he collapsed before the finish line, led to his disqualification for receiving assistance, with the victory awarded to Johnny Hayes.
events.name: Dorando Pietri's Olympic marathon

events.enhanced_description: On July 26, 1908, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) was founded in the United States. This agency was established to investigate and enforce federal laws, evolving into a key component of national security and law enforcement.
events.name: FBI founded

events.enhanced_description: On July 27, 1908, a devastating typhoon struck Hong Kong, sinking the passenger steamer Ying King and resulting in the deaths of 421 people. This disaster highlighted the vulnerability of maritime transport in severe weather conditions.

locations.name: Hong Kong, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

events.name: Hong Kong typhoon sinks Ying King

events.enhanced_description: On August 8, 1908, Wilbur Wright made his first flight in France, showcasing the capabilities of controlled powered flight. This event was significant in promoting aviation in Europe and solidifying the Wright brothers' legacy.
events.name: Wilbur Wright's flight in France

events.enhanced_description: On August 17, 1908, Émile Cohl's animated short film 'Fantasmagorie' was officially released. Widely regarded as the first animated cartoon, it marked a significant milestone in the history of animation and film.
events.name: Fantasmagorie released

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 1908, Sultan Abdelaziz of Morocco was deposed after a power struggle and succeeded by his brother Abd al-Hafid. This transition marked a significant change in Moroccan leadership during a period of political instability.

image.caption: Printed portrait of Sultan Abd el-Aziz published in Le Petit Journal.

events.enhanced_description: On August 28, 1908, the American Messenger Company was founded in Washington, D.C. This company would later evolve into the United Parcel Service (UPS), becoming a major player in the logistics and delivery industry.
events.name: American Messenger Company founded

events.enhanced_description: On August 31, 1908, the Great Storm of 1908 began to impact the Bristol Channel, causing significant damage and lasting until the morning of September 2. This storm was one of the most severe weather events of the year.
events.name: Great Storm of 1908

events.enhanced_description: On September 10, 1908, the Minas Geraes, the first Minas Geraes-class Dreadnought battleship for Brazil, was launched at Armstrong Whitworth's yard on the River Tyne in England. This event catalyzed the South American dreadnought race, significantly impacting naval power in the region.

locations.name: River Tyne, Newcastle upon Tyne, England

events.name: Minas Geraes launched

events.enhanced_description: On September 17, 1908, Thomas Selfridge became the first person to die in an airplane crash at Fort Myer, Virginia. The crash occurred during a demonstration flight piloted by Orville Wright, who sustained serious injuries but survived.

locations.name: Fort Myer, Arlington, Virginia, United States

events.name: First airplane crash fatality

events.enhanced_description: On September 28, 1908, classes began at the Benjamin Franklin Institute of Technology in Boston, Massachusetts. This institution was established under the terms of Benjamin Franklin's will, focusing on technical education.
events.name: Benjamin Franklin Institute of Technology classes begin

events.enhanced_description: On October 1, 1908, Henry Ford officially launched the Ford Model T automobile, which had its first unit leave the Ford Piquette Avenue Plant in Detroit on September 27. Priced at $850, the Model T revolutionized the automotive industry and made car ownership accessible to the masses.
events.name: Ford Model T launched

events.enhanced_description: On October 5, 1908, Bulgaria declared its independence from the Ottoman Empire, marking a significant moment in Balkan history. Ferdinand I, who had previously been a prince, was proclaimed Tsar, solidifying Bulgaria's status as a sovereign nation.
events.name: Bulgaria declares its independence from the Ottoman Empire; Ferdinand I of Bulgaria becomes Tsar

events.enhanced_description: The Bosnian crisis began on October 6, 1908, following the Austro-Hungarian Empire's annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, territories previously under Ottoman control. This act escalated tensions in the Balkans and contributed to the complex political landscape leading up to World War I.

locations.name: Sarajevo, Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.name: The Bosnian crisis begins, after the Austro-Hungarian Empire annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina from the Ottoman Empire

events.enhanced_description: On October 8, 1908, the University of Omaha was founded as a private non-sectarian college, which later evolved into the University of Nebraska Omaha. This institution played a significant role in higher education in the Midwest.
events.name: The University of Omaha, precursor of the University of Nebraska Omaha, is founded as a private non-sectarian college

events.enhanced_description: On October 14, 1908, the Chicago Cubs triumphed over the Detroit Tigers in the World Series, marking their second consecutive championship. This victory would be particularly notable as it would take the Cubs 108 years to win another title.
events.name: The Chicago Cubs beat the Detroit Tigers in the 1908 World Series in baseball

events.enhanced_description: On October 29, 1908, Olivetti was founded in Ivrea, Italy, by Camillo Olivetti. The company would become renowned for its innovative typewriters and later for its contributions to computing technology.
events.name: Olivetti, the well-known typewriter and business equipment company, is founded in Italy

events.enhanced_description: On November 3, 1908, William Howard Taft won the presidential election, defeating William Jennings Bryan with a significant electoral margin. This election was pivotal in shaping the future of the Republican Party and American politics.
events.name: 1908 United States presidential election: Republican candidate William Howard Taft defeats William Jennings Bryan

events.enhanced_description: On November 6, 1908, it was reported that notorious outlaws Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid were killed in Bolivia after being surrounded by soldiers. However, rumors persisted about their survival, adding to their legendary status in American folklore.
events.name: Western bandits Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid are supposedly killed in Bolivia

events.enhanced_description: On November 15, 1908, King Leopold II of Belgium officially transferred control of the Congo Free State to the Belgian government, following international outcry over human rights abuses. This marked the end of his personal rule and the beginning of the Belgian Congo.
events.name: King Leopold II of Belgium formally relinquishes his personal control of the Congo Free State

events.enhanced_description: The Christian Science Monitor was first published on November 25, 1908, in Boston, Massachusetts. It aimed to provide a balanced perspective on news and has since become known for its in-depth reporting and analysis.
events.name: The Christian Science Monitor newspaper is first published

events.enhanced_description: On December 2, 1908, Puyi ascended the throne of China at the tender age of two, becoming the last Emperor of the Qing Dynasty. His reign would be marked by significant political upheaval and the eventual fall of imperial rule in China.
events.name: Young Emperor Puyi ascends the Chinese throne at age 2

events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 1908, construction began on the RMS Olympic at the Harland and Wolff Shipyard in Belfast. The Olympic would go on to become one of the most famous ocean liners of her time, known for her luxury and size.
events.name: Construction begins on the RMS Olympic

events.enhanced_description: On December 23, 1908, a hybrid solar eclipse was visible from the Atlantic Ocean, marking the 23rd solar eclipse of Solar Saros 140. This astronomical event was significant for scientists and skywatchers alike.

image.caption: Map showing the path of the December 23, 1908 hybrid solar eclipse.
image.credit: Attribution: Eclipse Predictions by Fred Espenak, NASA's GSFC — http://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/
image.date_qualification: The map depicts the 1908 eclipse; image_date is recorded as 2000, not as the eclipse date.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: A hybrid solar eclipse is visible from the Atlantic Ocean

events.enhanced_description: On December 28, 1908, a devastating 7.1 Mw earthquake struck Messina, Sicily, resulting in a catastrophic loss of life, with estimates ranging from 75,000 to 200,000 fatalities. This disaster had profound effects on the region and led to significant changes in building regulations.
events.name: The 7.1 Mw Messina earthquake shakes Southern Italy

events.enhanced_description: In 1909, Karl Landsteiner, Constantin Levaditi, and Erwin Popper successfully isolated the poliovirus for the first time. This groundbreaking discovery laid the foundation for future research and the development of vaccines against poliomyelitis.
events.name: Isolation of the Poliovirus

events.enhanced_description: The RMS Republic, a White Star Line ocean liner, sank off the coast of Nantucket after colliding with the SS Florida. This incident marked one of the first maritime disasters to receive extensive media coverage, highlighting the dangers of early 20th-century sea travel.
events.name: The sinking of RMS Republic

events.enhanced_description: The withdrawal of the last United States troops from Cuba marked the end of American military presence following the Spanish-American War. This event was significant in the context of U.S.-Cuban relations and the broader implications of American imperialism in the Caribbean.
events.name: Last United States troops leave Cuba

events.enhanced_description: The Paris Film Congress convened to discuss the establishment of a European film cartel, aiming to unify leading producers in response to the dominance of the American film industry. This event was pivotal in shaping the future of European cinema.
events.name: The Paris Film Congress opens

events.enhanced_description: Leo Baekeland announced the creation of Bakelite, the first synthetic plastic, which revolutionized materials science and manufacturing. This invention paved the way for the development of numerous plastic products that are ubiquitous today.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Announcement of Bakelite

events.enhanced_description: William Howard Taft was inaugurated as the 27th President of the United States, succeeding Theodore Roosevelt. His presidency would later be marked by significant political challenges and the eventual split in the Republican Party.
events.name: Inauguration of William Howard Taft

events.enhanced_description: The Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 was signed in Bangkok, establishing borders between British Malaya and Siam (now Thailand). This treaty was crucial in defining the territorial limits of Siam and reducing British influence in the region.
events.name: Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909

events.enhanced_description: Einar Dessau successfully used a shortwave radio transmitter in Denmark, marking a significant advancement in radio technology. This innovation contributed to the development of long-distance communication methods.
events.name: Einar Dessau uses shortwave radio transmitter

events.enhanced_description: The remains of the Báb, a central figure in the Bahá'í faith, were placed in the Bahá'í Shrine on Mount Carmel in Haifa. This event is significant in Bahá'í history, symbolizing the establishment of a sacred site for followers.
events.name: Remains of the Báb placed in Bahá'í Shrine

events.enhanced_description: Serbia's acceptance of Austrian control over Bosnia and Herzegovina was a pivotal moment in Balkan politics, reflecting the tensions between Serbia and Austria-Hungary that would later contribute to the outbreak of World War I.
events.name: Serbia accepts Austrian control over Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.enhanced_description: Construction of the RMS Titanic began at the Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast, marking the start of what would become one of the most famous ocean liners in history. The Titanic was designed to be the largest and most luxurious ship of its time.
events.name: Construction begins on the RMS Titanic

events.enhanced_description: Sport Club Internacional was founded in Porto Alegre, Brazil, becoming one of the most successful football clubs in the country. The club has a rich history and a passionate fan base, contributing significantly to Brazilian football culture.

locations.name: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

events.name: Founding of Sport Club Internacional

events.enhanced_description: Robert Peary, Matthew Henson, and four Inuit explorers came within a few miles of the North Pole, marking a significant achievement in Arctic exploration. Their journey contributed to the understanding of polar regions and the challenges of extreme environments.

image.caption: Robert E. Peary’s diary entry from his polar expeditions.
image.credit: Robert Peary — U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
image.date_qualification: The supplied image date identifies 6 April 1909; it is not an upload date. The record describes a diary entry, not an event photograph.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Peary's expedition near the North Pole

events.enhanced_description: The city of Tel Aviv was founded by the Jewish community on the outskirts of Jaffa, marking a significant moment in the establishment of modern Israeli urban centers. Initially known as Ahuzat Bayit, it has grown to become a major cultural and economic hub.

locations.name: Tel Aviv, Tel Aviv District, Israel

events.name: Founding of Tel Aviv

events.enhanced_description: A countercoup began in the Ottoman Empire, reflecting the political turmoil and struggles for power within the empire. This event was part of a larger context of reform and resistance during the late Ottoman period.
events.name: Countercoup in the Ottoman Empire

events.enhanced_description: The Adana massacre resulted in the deaths of 15,000 to 30,000 Armenian Christians at the hands of Ottoman Turks, highlighting the ethnic tensions and violence that characterized the late Ottoman Empire. This tragic event is a significant part of Armenian history.
events.name: Adana massacre

events.enhanced_description: Joan of Arc was beatified in Rome, recognizing her as a martyr and a saint in the Catholic Church. This event underscored her significance in both religious and national contexts, particularly in France.

image.caption: Albert Lynch’s painting Jeanne d’Arc, a portrait of Joan of Arc.
image.credit: Albert Lynch — [1]
image.date_qualification: Created in 1901, before the beatification on 1909-04-18; this is a retrospective portrait, not a contemporary event image.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Beatification of Joan of Arc

events.enhanced_description: The Anglo-Persian Oil Company, which would later become BP, was incorporated in London. This marked a significant development in the global oil industry and the economic relationships between Britain and Persia.
events.name: Incorporation of Anglo-Persian Oil Company

events.enhanced_description: Sultan Abdul Hamid II was overthrown in a coup and succeeded by his brother Mehmed V, marking a significant shift in the Ottoman Empire's political landscape. This event was part of the broader Young Turk Revolution that aimed to modernize and reform the empire.
events.name: Overthrow of Sultan Abdul Hamid II

events.enhanced_description: The Ballets Russes, produced by Sergei Diaghilev, opened a tour at the Théâtre du Châtelet in Paris, introducing Russian ballet to Western audiences. This event significantly influenced the development of modern ballet and performance art.
events.name: Ballets Russes tour in Western world

events.enhanced_description: French forces captured Abéché, the capital of the Wadai Empire in central Africa, during their colonial expansion. This event was part of France's efforts to establish control over territories in Africa.
events.name: Capture of Abéché by French forces

events.enhanced_description: Representatives from England, Australia, and South Africa met at Lord's Cricket Ground in London to form the Imperial Cricket Conference, which would later evolve into the International Cricket Council (ICC). This event was crucial in the development of international cricket.
events.name: Formation of the Imperial Cricket Conference

events.enhanced_description: Indian nationalist student Madan Lal Dhingra assassinated Curzon Wyllie, a political aide to the Secretary of State for India, in London. This act of violence was a significant moment in the Indian nationalist movement, reflecting growing tensions against British rule.

image.caption: Portrait of Madan Lal Dhingra.
image.credit: Punjab state archives
image.date_qualification: Portrait of the assassin discussed in the article; it is not a depiction of the 1909 assassination. Image date is stated as before 1960.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Assassination of Curzon Wyllie

events.enhanced_description: A revolution forced Mohammad Ali Shah of the Qajar dynasty to abdicate in favor of his son Ahmad Shah Qajar, marking a significant shift in Iranian politics. This event was part of the broader constitutional revolution in Persia.

image.caption: Portrait of Mohammad Ali Shah Qajar in military uniform wearing the Kayanid Crown.
image.credit: Abdollah Mirza Qajar — The Nelson Collection
image.date_qualification: Portrait dated circa 1907, before his abdication on 16 July 1909; it is not a depiction of the abdication event.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Abdication of Mohammad Ali Shah

events.enhanced_description: On July 25, 1909, Louis Blériot made history by completing the first successful crossing of the English Channel in a manned airplane. This landmark achievement marked a significant milestone in aviation and showcased the potential of powered flight.
events.name: 1909 Channel crossing

events.enhanced_description: Louis Blériot became the first person to fly across the English Channel in a heavier-than-air aircraft, demonstrating the potential of aviation. This historic flight marked a significant milestone in the development of flight and aviation technology.
events.name: Louis Blériot flies across the English Channel

events.enhanced_description: The city of Barcelona experienced a workers' uprising known as 'Tragic Week' (La Semana Trágica), which was marked by violent protests against the Spanish government. This event highlighted the social tensions and labor struggles in early 20th-century Spain.
events.name: Tragic Week in Barcelona

events.enhanced_description: The SS Waratah, a passenger and cargo liner of the Blue Anchor Line, vanished on its second voyage from Australia to Britain after departing from Durban. All 211 people aboard were lost, and the ship's disappearance remains one of the great maritime mysteries.
events.name: Loss of SS Waratah

events.enhanced_description: On August 2, 1909, the United States Army Signal Corps made a historic purchase of the Wright Military Flyer from the Wright brothers, marking the first acquisition of a military airplane. This event signified the beginning of military aviation in the United States.
events.name: Purchase of the Wright Military Flyer

events.enhanced_description: Max Heindel formally established the Rosicrucian Fellowship in Seattle on August 8, 1909, aiming to promote spiritual development and esoteric knowledge. This organization has since played a significant role in the Rosicrucian movement.
events.name: Founding of the Rosicrucian Fellowship

events.enhanced_description: On September 4, 1909, Japan and China signed the Gando Convention, which allowed Japan to secure railroad concessions in Manchuria. This agreement was part of Japan's broader imperial ambitions in East Asia.
events.name: Signing of the Gando Convention

events.enhanced_description: In October 1909, Suzuki Weaving Machine Manufacturing was founded in Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan. This company would eventually evolve into the well-known Suzuki motorbike and automobile brand.
events.name: Founding of Suzuki Weaving Machine Manufacturing

events.enhanced_description: Following an earthquake in the Zagreb area on October 8, 1909, geologist Andrija Mohorovičić identified the boundary between the Earth's crust and the underlying mantle, now known as the Mohorovičić discontinuity. This discovery has had lasting implications in the field of geology.
events.name: Identification of the Mohorovičić Discontinuity

events.enhanced_description: On October 12, 1909, Coritiba Football Club was founded in Curitiba, Brazil. It has since become one of the most prominent football clubs in Brazil, contributing significantly to the country's rich football culture.
events.name: Founding of Coritiba Football Club

events.enhanced_description: On October 13, 1909, an agreement was reached between Germany, Italy, and Switzerland, granting access to the Gotthard Rail Tunnel for German and Italian trains. This agreement facilitated transportation and trade across the Alpine region.
events.name: Access Agreement for Gotthard Rail Tunnel

events.enhanced_description: On October 16, 1909, the Pittsburgh Pirates triumphed over the Detroit Tigers to win the 1909 World Series. This victory marked the Pirates' first championship since 1903 and solidified their place in baseball history.

events.enhanced_description: On October 26, 1909, Itō Hirobumi, a prominent Japanese statesman and four-time Prime Minister, was assassinated by An Jung-geun, a Korean independence activist, at the Harbin railway station. This event had significant repercussions for Japanese-Korean relations.

events.enhanced_description: On November 18, 1909, dictator José Santos Zelaya ordered the execution of 500 revolutionaries, including two Americans, in Nicaragua. This brutal crackdown prompted the United States to respond by sending two warships to the region.
events.name: Execution of Revolutionaries in Nicaragua

events.enhanced_description: On November 28, 1909, Sergei Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 3 premiered in New York City, with the composer himself as the soloist. This work has since become one of the most celebrated and technically challenging pieces in the piano repertoire.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Premiere of Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 3

events.enhanced_description: On December 4, 1909, the Montreal Canadiens, one of the most storied franchises in professional ice hockey, were founded in Montreal, Canada. The team has since become a symbol of Canadian hockey culture.
events.name: Founding of the Montreal Canadiens

events.enhanced_description: On December 14, 1909, New South Wales Premier Charles Wade signed the Seat of Government Surrender Act, completing the transfer of land to the Commonwealth to establish the Australian Capital Territory. This act was pivotal in the development of Australia's national capital.
events.name: Seat of Government Surrender Act 1909

events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 1909, Borussia Dortmund was founded in Dortmund, Germany. The club has since grown to become one of the most successful and popular football teams in Germany and Europe.
events.name: Founding of Borussia Dortmund

events.enhanced_description: On December 23, 1909, Albert I ascended to the throne of Belgium following the death of his uncle, King Leopold II. His reign would be marked by significant events, including World War I and the modernization of Belgium.
events.name: Ascension of King Albert I of Belgium

events.enhanced_description: On December 28, 1909, French aviator Albert Kimmerling made the first manned heavier-than-air powered flight in South Africa at East London, flying a Voisin 1907 biplane. This event marked a significant milestone in the history of aviation in the region.

locations.name: East London, Eastern Cape, South Africa

events.name: First Manned Flight in South Africa

events.enhanced_description: In early 1910, American-born physician Hawley Harvey Crippen poisoned his wife, Cora, and concealed her body in the cellar of their home in London. This shocking crime led to a sensational trial that captivated the public and raised questions about domestic violence and the legal system.
events.name: Hawley Harvey Crippen's Crime

events.enhanced_description: In 1910, the Nazareth Baptist Church, an African-initiated church, was founded by Prophet Isaiah Shembe in South Africa. This church played a significant role in the spiritual and cultural life of many South Africans.
events.name: Founding of Nazareth Baptist Church

events.enhanced_description: Sport Club Corinthians Paulista was founded in São Paulo, Brazil, by a group of railway workers. The club has since become one of the most successful football teams in Brazil and was the first to win the FIFA Club World Cup in 2000.
events.name: Foundation of Sport Club Corinthians Paulista

events.enhanced_description: In 1910, electric streetcars became a significant mode of urban transportation in Austria-Hungary, France, Germany, and Great Britain, carrying approximately 6.7 million riders annually. This advancement marked a pivotal shift in public transport, enhancing urban mobility and contributing to the growth of cities.

locations.name: Austria-Hungary, France, Germany and Great Britain

events.name: The electric streetcars of Austria-Hungary, France, Germany and Great Britain are carrying 6.7 million riders per year.

events.enhanced_description: In 1910, Henry Ford achieved a significant milestone by selling 10,000 automobiles, showcasing the success of his assembly line production methods. This event not only revolutionized the automotive industry but also made cars more accessible to the general public, fundamentally changing transportation in America.
events.name: Henry Ford sells 10,000 automobiles.

events.enhanced_description: In 1910, Hitachi was established in Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan, originally as a mining machine repair factory. Over the years, it evolved into a global leader in various sectors, including electronics and infrastructure, significantly impacting Japan's industrial landscape.
events.name: Hitachi, an electromechanics company, is founded as a mining machine repair factory in Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan.

events.enhanced_description: On January 6, 1910, the Abé people in the French colony of Côte d'Ivoire rose against colonial rule. The rebellion was brutally suppressed by the French military, highlighting the tensions between colonial powers and indigenous populations.
events.name: Abé Rebellion in Côte d'Ivoire

events.enhanced_description: On January 8, 1910, the Treaty of Punakha was signed, establishing Bhutan as a protectorate of the British Empire. This treaty marked a significant shift in Bhutan's foreign relations and its status in the region.
events.name: Treaty of Punakha

events.enhanced_description: On January 11, 1910, French explorer Jean-Baptiste Charcot discovered Charcot Island during his Antarctic expedition aboard the ship Pourquoi Pas?. This discovery contributed to the understanding of the Antarctic region.
events.name: Discovery of Charcot Island

events.enhanced_description: The Great January Comet of 1910 was first observed on January 12, 1910, with its perihelion occurring on January 17. This comet was notable for its brightness and visibility.
events.name: Observation of the Great January Comet

events.enhanced_description: The Great Flood of Paris began on January 21, 1910, when the Seine River overflowed its banks, leading to significant flooding in the city. This disaster caused widespread damage and prompted emergency responses.
events.name: Great Flood of Paris

events.enhanced_description: On January 22, 1910, the completion of the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company Tower in New York City was celebrated. At 700 feet, it was the tallest building in the world at the time, symbolizing the architectural ambitions of the era.

locations.name: New York City, New York, United States

events.name: Completion of Metropolitan Life Insurance Company Tower

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1910, a catastrophic explosion occurred at the Colorado Fuel and Iron Company coal mine in Primero, Colorado, resulting in the tragic deaths of 75 miners. This disaster highlighted the perilous conditions faced by laborers in the mining industry during this period.
events.name: Primero Coal Mine Explosion

events.enhanced_description: On February 1, 1910, a coal mine explosion at the Browder Coal Company in Drakesboro, Kentucky, resulted in the deaths of 34 miners. This incident underscored the dangerous working conditions prevalent in the mining industry during the early 20th century.
events.name: Drakesboro Coal Mine Explosion

events.enhanced_description: On February 2, 1910, a devastating explosion at the Palau mine in Las Esperanzas, Coahuila, Mexico, claimed the lives of 68 miners. This tragedy highlighted the ongoing risks associated with coal mining in Mexico during this era.
events.name: Palau Mine Explosion

events.enhanced_description: On February 5, 1910, an explosion at the Jefferson Clearfield Coal Company mine in Ernest, Pennsylvania, resulted in the deaths of 11 miners, primarily of Hungarian descent, while 110 others managed to escape. This incident was part of a series of mining disasters that plagued the industry.
events.name: Ernest Coal Mine Explosion
